newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt to sell Turkey 7.3 mln tonnes LNG.
newsitem.headline: Egypt to sell Turkey 7.3 mln tonnes LNG.

text.p: Egyptian Oil Minister Hamdi el-Banbi announced on Wednesday Egypt had reached an agreement to export up to 7.3 million tonnes of liquefied natural gas (LNG) to Turkey by the year 2000.

"We have reached a memorandum of understanding between the Egyptian General Petroleum Corporation and Turkey's Botas and (U.S. firm) Amoco Corp (Corp) to export and sell Turkey 10 billion cubic metres or 7.3 million tonnes of LNG a year," he told a session of the Middle East and North Africa Economic Conference.
"The project will be finished by the year 2000 and estimated costs are between $2 billion and $4 billion. (Italian energy firm) ENI SpA has agreed to take part," Banbi added.
Egypt has originally planned to export gas first to Israel, through a pipeline crossing the Gaza Strip.
But in an interview published in al-Ahram on Sunday, Banbi said gas export negotiations with Turkey were more advanced than those with Israel.
ENI and Amoco have been working closely in Egypt's natural gas fields in and off the Nile Delta.
